target.title: fix(cli): exit cleanly on startup migration refusal
target.body:
## Summary

- report the three planned startup migration/config/plugin refusal reasons at their owner, then throw `ExitError(1)` so `ensureConfigReady` uses its existing typed `runtime.exit` path
- add a hermetic child-process regression that exercises a real conflicting plugin-state migration, requires exit status 1 with no signal, verifies the refusal appears exactly once, and confirms the startup migration lease is released
- audit the core `DatabaseSync` migration/checkpoint paths for throw-time handle leaks; every direct handle is already closed by `finally`, so no unrelated migration refactor is included

This PR is stacked on #110200 (base commit `ce6e200aaa2`) because that PR separated the three refusal cases. #110200 remains open, so this PR should still land after it.

Refs #109831.

## What Problem This Solves

Startup migration, invalid-config, and plugin-verification refusals were ordinary `Error`s. They bypassed the typed exit handling in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`, reached the generic `src/entry.ts` failure handler, and ended in its direct `process.exit(1)` path. In the reported supervised deployment, that path terminated with signal 11 / status 139 instead of a clean refusal status, turning a fail-closed migration result into a supervisor crash loop.

## Root Cause

The proven pre-fix control flow is:

1. `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` formatted an intentional readiness refusal but threw a plain `Error`.
2. `ensureConfigReady` only converts `ExitError` into `runtime.exit(error.code)`, so it rethrew the plain refusal.
3. `src/entry.ts` added `Could not start the CLI.` / `Reason:` formatting and called `process.exit(1)`.

The preflight's existing `finally` already releases its heartbeat and startup migration lease before the error leaves the owner. The fix preserves that unwind and hands the intentional refusal to the typed caller contract instead of treating it as an unexpected CLI startup failure.

The reporter's exact native signal source is not established without their core dump. This change fixes the incorrect refusal path and locks down the observable process contract; it does not claim to identify or patch the native module.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal owner must print the reason because the typed `ExitError` branch intentionally does not format errors, while the generic entry catch is no longer reached. Printing once immediately before throwing `ExitError(1)` preserves the complete operator guidance without duplicating the generic wrapper.

This is the narrow owner-boundary fix: unexpected preflight errors still use the generic failure handler, and gateway readiness remains fail-closed.

The core migration audit covered the direct `DatabaseSync` constructors in `src/infra/state-migrations.debug-proxy.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.task-sidecar-rows.ts`, and `src/infra/state-migrations.storage.ts`, plus the checkpoint database wrapper used by `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.ts`. Each closes in `finally`, including throw paths. No plugin-owned code was changed.

## User Impact

When a startup migration gate refuses readiness, operators retain the full actionable refusal text exactly once. The CLI exits through the typed status-1 path, the migration lease is released, and supervisors see a normal non-zero exit rather than a signal in the covered regression environment.

## Evidence

### Guard-boundary verification

ClawSweeper's first review reported that the `ExitError` bridge was missing. Direct inspection shows the bridge already exists on both this PR head and the exact live-main revision reviewed by ClawSweeper (`d957b157e049`):

```ts
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ExitError) {
    // The migration owner has unwound its lease and heartbeat before this handoff.
    params.runtime.exit(error.code);
  }
  throw error;
}
```

The live process transcript below independently proves this branch reaches that bridge: the generic entry wrapper is absent after the patch and present on the merge-base source.

### Real behavior proof

Environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, actual `src/entry.ts`, no provider/channel credentials, isolated realpathed `HOME`, config, and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The fixture contains a canonical plugin-state row and a legacy `plugin-state/state.sqlite` row with the same key but divergent values, so migration intentionally leaves the sidecar unresolved. The wrapper uses GNU `timeout` as a supervisor boundary and captures the child wait status plus stdout/stderr separately.

Exact gateway invocation, repeated against the same unresolved state:

```text
env -i PATH=<PATH> HOME=<TMP> USERPROFILE=<TMP> \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<TMP>/openclaw.json \
  OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 \
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<TMP>/state OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 NO_COLOR=1 \
  timeout --signal=KILL 60s node --import tsx src/entry.ts \
  gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

Observed supervisor and lease results:

```text
gateway_run_1 status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_run_1 active_startup_migration_lease=false
gateway_run_2 status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_run_2 active_startup_migration_lease=false
```

Redacted stderr from both runs was identical:

```text
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row already existed in shared state: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row already existed in shared state: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

This establishes status 1 rather than signal 11/status 139, one refusal headline on stderr, no generic outer-entry wrapper, and lease release before a second supervised attempt. The second run acquired a fresh lease and reproduced the intended refusal instead of reporting `OpenClaw startup migrations are already running`.

### Doctor-path parity

The same unresolved fixture was passed through the actual doctor entry path:

```text
timeout --signal=KILL 60s node --import tsx src/entry.ts \
  doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
```

Observed comparison:

```text
pre_fix_doctor status=0 signal=none
branch_doctor status=0 signal=none
doctor_migration_stderr_identical=yes

[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row already existed in shared state: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key

after_doctor_fix active_startup_migration_lease=false
gateway_after_doctor status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_after_doctor active_startup_migration_lease=false
```

Doctor does not gate gateway readiness, so its expected contract remains a normal status-0 report of the unresolved migration. Its migration stderr is identical before and after this patch. A gateway start after doctor still takes the clean typed refusal path, proving the change does not hide or incorrectly repair the fail-closed condition.

### Merge-base contrast

For a cheap before comparison, the same fixture and supervisor command were run from an archive of merge base `433b3ce86d71a88fb34d4f61f6f10c36b912aeee` with the current dependency install:

```text
pre_fix status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 generic_wrapper_count=1

[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row already existed in shared state: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row already existed in shared state: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
[openclaw] Debug: set OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1 to include the stack trace.
[openclaw] Try: openclaw doctor
[openclaw] Help: openclaw --help
```

The reporter's SIGSEGV did not reproduce on this host on either revision. The observed before/after difference is the contract this PR owns: merge-base reaches the generic entry failure formatter, while this branch reaches the existing typed config-guard exit and emits only the owner-rendered refusal. Identifying the reporter's crashing native module remains deferred pending their core dump.

### Focused regression proof

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       24 passed (24)
Duration    3.39s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.38s
```

### Verification

- `pnpm format src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts` — passed (`Finished in 6ms on 2 files`)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts` — 2 files passed, 24 tests passed
- `git diff --check $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)..HEAD` — passed
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts src/cli/program/config-guard.ts` — Testbox delegation was blocked because the host Blacksmith client was not authenticated; the policy-permitted trusted-source local fallback then passed all scoped checks. It emitted one warning-only suggestion to migrate the existing process test to the shared temp-directory helper.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted ...` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings, overall patch correctness 0.94

## What Was Not Tested

- The reporter's exact container/supervisor/native-module failure was not reproduced; identifying the crashing native module requires the reporter's core dump and is intentionally deferred.
- No successful full gateway channel/provider startup was exercised. The real child process stops at the intended preflight refusal, before `runGatewayCommand` starts runtime services.
- No broad suite was run; focused coverage exercises the changed refusal owner, existing migration cases, child-process exit semantics, lease cleanup, and the scoped core changed gate.
